title: Howard Hughes in Las Vegas
summary: Josh and Chuck profile Howard Hughes's years in Las Vegas, from his 1966 arrival and four-year stay on the ninth floor of the Desert Inn, through his purchase of Vegas hotel-casinos, his germophobia and OCD, his aides (including Robert Mayhew and the Mormon Mafia), his 1970 departure to the Bahamas, and his 1976 death and estate. The episode opens with a sponsor/friend shout-out and closes with listener mail correcting a kangaroo-etymology myth and a movie-recommendation banter.
topics: Arthur Ashe Desert Inn tennis tournament
Baskin Robbins banana ripple ice cream

segments.title: Opening banter and friends' podcast shout-out
segments.summary: Hosts plug Ben Harrison and Adam Pranica's independent Greatest Generation podcast and their Supercast membership, joke about the Cheesecake Factory's from-scratch cooking, and tease the episode.

segments.title: Howard Hughes background and aviation/film ventures
segments.summary: Hughes's Houston origins, oil-drill fortune, inheritance at 18, founding of Hughes Aircraft, control of TWA and RKO, celebrity status, and his plane crash injuries. Hosts also discuss The Aviator as a Vegas-era portrayal.

segments.title: Hughes's opioid addiction and decline
segments.summary: Hughes became dependent on morphine after his injuries, stopped appearing in public by 1961, lost weight and height, and his mental decline was linked to his wealth and public adoration.

segments.title: Hughes's germophobia and early interest in Vegas
segments.summary: Hughes's germ fears, poor hygiene, bottled water only, and his 1966 arrival in Vegas to take advantage of a tax shelter after selling TWA stock. Vegas was then a mob-run town that respectable businesses avoided.

segments.title: Arrival at the Desert Inn ninth floor
segments.summary: Hughes came for a planned short stay, was secretly moved to the ninth floor of the Desert Inn, and stayed for years, blacking out windows and isolating himself.

segments.title: Hughes's diet, Baskin-Robbins order, and tissue rituals
segments.summary: Malnutrition and anemia from sweets; the Baskin-Robbins banana ripple ice cream special order; his twelve-step can-opening instructions; tissue use; and a photo of him wearing tissue boxes as shoes, which the hosts discuss.

segments.title: Robert Mayhew and the Mormon Mafia aides
segments.summary: Robert Mayhew ran Hughes's affairs and never met him in person; six men known as the Mormon Mafia carried out orders, handled tissues and morphine, and Hughes avoided bathrooms other people had used.

segments.title: Hughes's urine saving and TV station purchase
segments.summary: Hughes reportedly saved his urine and feces in bottles; he bought a local Las Vegas TV station to program movies, reportedly having films restarted, and favored aerial combat films and Ice Station Zebra. Hosts digress into favorite movies and a recommendation of Onyx.

segments.title: Hosts' movie banter and book recommendation
segments.summary: Hosts chat about films they have seen most, recommending the Oral History of Dazed and Confused, and other movie references.

segments.title: Hotel eviction threat and Hughes buys the Desert Inn
segments.summary: Management wanted the floor for New Year's Eve; Mayhew said Hughes would buy the hotel, and Hughes bought it for about $13.25 million, entering the hotel-casino business.

segments.title: Hughes's casino purchases and vision for a city of the future
segments.summary: Hughes bought the Sands, Castaways, Silver Slipper, Landmark, and Frontier from 1966 to 1968, envisioned a smogless, efficient respectable Vegas, and pushed a list of proposals including repealing taxes, keeping dog racing illegal, and cleaning up water. The Nevada Corporate Gaming Act eased public company entry.
topics: Las Vegas city of the future

segments.title: Hughes's racism, Arthur Ashe tournament, and antitrust action
segments.summary: Hughes's documented racism and abusive behavior, his attempt to cancel the 1968 Desert Inn tennis tournament because Arthur Ashe was competing, Ashe winning the singles title, and a federal antitrust suit blocking a seventh casino.

segments.title: Competition with Kerkorian and the Landmark grand opening
segments.summary: Kirk Kerkorian's International Hotel was planned to be the largest hotel; Hughes tried to stop it, then staged a rival grand opening for the Landmark, which was too small to be profitable. Timing of the Landmark purchase is discussed.

segments.title: Mob skimming and Hughes's departure to the Bahamas
segments.summary: The mob skimmed about fifty million dollars from Hughes's casinos; he left Vegas in November 1970 by stretcher and flew to the Bahamas. Hosts compare the film's depiction with what is known about his few departures from his room.

segments.title: Hughes's death, lack of will, and estate
segments.summary: Hughes died April 5, 1976 on a flight from Mexico to Houston at age 70, weighing 93 pounds; cause listed as kidney failure with codeine present; no will, many fake wills surfaced; estate of about $2.5 billion split among claimants. Mayhew was let go; the land became Summerlin.

segments.title: Psychological autopsy by Raymond Fowler
segments.summary: Estate claimants hired an attorney who engaged Raymond Fowler to conduct a psychological autopsy; research sources and the conclusion that Hughes had OCD, possibly rooted in his mother's polio-related germ fears. Hosts note the lack of documentaries on the Vegas years.

segments.title: Listener mail: kangaroo etymology myth
segments.summary: A listener from Albuquerque, Benjamin, writes in about the kangaroo word-origin myth, citing the film Arrival as a possible source; hosts discuss it and thank Australian listeners who corrected them.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and give the iHeartRadio credit and listener contact information.
